ruled_out_vectors.vector: Malicious pool type returns inflated amountOut to steal from LPs
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Core validates: L1405 actualAmountIn <= originalAmountIn, _safeDecrementUint128 output <= reserves, L2208 balance check. Three independent guards prevent extraction.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Malicious transfer handler skips actual token transfer
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Core verifies actual balance change at L2208: balanceInBefore + amountIn != balanceInAfter triggers revert. Handler cannot lie about token transfers.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Malicious hook returns inflated fee to extract from swappers
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook fees are BPS-based (fee = amount * feeBPS / 10000), bounded by MAX_BPS. Hooks are set by token owners via setTokenSettings. Third parties cannot install malicious hooks. Self-inflicted high fees = by-design.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Pool type address collision via 6-leading-zero-bytes address
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool IDs include pool type address. createPool checks poolInitialized[poolId] for duplicates. Different pool type addresses => different poolIds. No collision risk.
SecureProxy uses custom pattern (not UUPS/beacon). secureUpgrade requires SECURE_PROXY_ADMIN_ROLE + TIER_ADMIN pause. Constructor atomically initializes.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Diamond selector collision — malicious pool type selector collides with admin function
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: LimitBreakAMM uses explicit delegation (delegateCallPure per function), NOT selector-based routing. Pool types are called via external call, not through diamond proxy.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: CREATE2 redeploy different code at trusted pool type address
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool types are stateless computation contracts — they don't hold funds. Pool state is in AMM diamond storage. Redeploying at a pool type address could affect new pools but not extract from existing ones.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: AMMModule.sol:1389,1548 (external call to pool type, state in diamond storage)

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Malicious facet writes to shared diamond storage slot
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool types are called via CALL (not delegatecall) — they CANNOT write to AMM storage. Only ModuleLiquidity/ModuleAdmin/ModuleFeeCollection use delegatecall and are admin-deployed.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Bypass facet management to add malicious facet without governance
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SecureProxy has no dynamic facet addition (no diamond cut). Implementation set atomically via secureUpgrade (requires SECURE_PROXY_ADMIN_ROLE + full pause).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Reentrancy during hook fee distribution (flags cleared at L3190)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) preserves ENTERED bit (TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol:69-71). Custom flags cleared but ENTERED guard remains. Reentrant calls to swap/liquidity functions revert.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Transient storage cross-path — DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT read by addLiquidity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Only read site is afterSwap direct path in _validatePricingBounds. validateAddLiquidity uses getCurrentPriceX96 (pool type external call, not transient). Reentrancy guard prevents concurrent operations.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Hook/pool accounting desync (Bunni $8.3M pattern) — beforeSwap state persists after afterSwap revert
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMStandardHook has NO internal balance accounting. beforeSwap/afterSwap only validate trading rules and compute fees (pure BPS). No state changes that could desync. EVM atomicity: if afterSwap reverts, entire swap reverts.

_executeTransferHandlerCallback runs AFTER balance check (L2208) and output disbursement (L2235-2244). CLOBTransferHandler.afterSwapRefund only transfers CLOB's own tokens to executor, checks msg.sender==AMM. Reentrancy guard active. Cannot manipulate AMM state.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Operator precedence in registryUpdatePricingBounds silently disables min-only bounds
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMStandardHook.sol:567 `minSqrtPriceX96 | maxSqrtPriceX96 == 0` has precedence issue (== binds tighter than |). When max=0 (min-only bound), expression evaluates as `min | 1 = truthy` entering unset branch. But: only callable by registry (token owner), informational self-configuration issue, not exploitable by third parties.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Fee collection cross-contamination between hook-managed and token-managed pools
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook-managed fees use key hash(hookAddress, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)). Token-managed fees use key hash(TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)). collectHookFeesByHook requires msg.sender==hook. collectHookFeesByToken requires token owner role. Different keys prevent cross-pool access.

lens_coverage.lens1_value_tracing: Traced fee computation through all four fee paths: _applySwapByInputInputFees (input token hook fees on input), _applySwapByInputOutputFees (output token hook fees on output), _applySwapByOutputInputFees (hook fees added to input for output-based), _applySwapByOutputOutputFees (hook fees added to output for output-based). Verified token_used_in_transfer == token_used_in_computation for all paths. Pool types return fees in input token denomination, transferred in same denomination. Fee collection keys (hook-managed vs token-managed) correctly partition storage.
lens_coverage.lens2_paired_op_diffing: Compared addLiquidity vs removeLiquidity hook validation. Both call same access control pattern (_requireCallerIsAMM). validateRemoveLiquidity is pure (no state changes). validateCollectFees always reverts (no fee collection hooks). No asymmetries found. Compared collectHookFeesByHook vs collectHookFeesByToken: different key derivation (hook address vs TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE sentinel), different access control (msg.sender==hook vs token owner role), no cross-contamination.
lens_coverage.lens3_amplification: No denomination mismatch found. All fee/amount values traced from computation to consumption use consistent token denomination. Transfer handler callback (afterSwapRefund) only transfers handler's own tokens, cannot amplify. Hook fee queue uses transient storage with deterministic slot calculation, no amplification possible.
